items.title: Complex $L^\infty$ space of a locally compact group
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$
([[def-left-haar-integral-and-left-haar-measure]]). Use the complex-valued
measurability convention and modulus from
[[def-complex-haar-lp-spaces-and-compactly-supported-functions]]. For a Borel
measurable $f:G\to\mathbb C$, set
$$\|f\|_{\infty,\mu}:=\inf\{t>0:\mu(\{x\in G:|f(x)|>t\})=0\},$$
with infimum $+\infty$ when the set of such $t$ is empty. Let
$\mathcal L^\infty(G,\mu;\mathbb C)$ be the complex measurable functions with
finite $\|f\|_{\infty,\mu}$, identify $f\sim g$ when $f=g$ $\mu$-almost
everywhere, and write
$$L^\infty(G,\mu;\mathbb C):=\{[f]:f\in\mathcal L^\infty(G,\mu;\mathbb C)\}.$$
Addition and complex scalar multiplication are $[f]+[g]=[f+g]$ and
$\alpha[f]=[\alpha f]$, and the norm is $\|[f]\|_\infty:=\|f\|_{\infty,\mu}$.
This is the complex $L^\infty$ space used on the amenability page; its
functions are equivalence classes, not chosen representatives.
items.strategy: Representatives differing almost everywhere give the same pointwise operations and essential supremum. Real and imaginary parts of sums and complex scalar multiples remain measurable. The essential-supremum threshold sets give closure under addition and scalar multiplication, the triangle inequality by |f+g|<=|f|+|g| and homogeneity by scaling. If the essential supremum is zero, each set {|f|>1/n} is null; their countable union is null and f vanishes outside it. This proves the class operations are well-defined and the displayed quantity is a norm. No use of Choice.

items.title: Left-invariant means on $L^\infty$ of a locally compact group
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$.
Write $L^\infty(G):=L^\infty(G,\mu;\mathbb C)$ for the complex a.e.-class
space of [[def-complex-haar-l-infinity-space]]. For $g\in G$ define the left
translate by
$$L_gf(x):=f(g^{-1}x).$$
It is well defined on classes and isometric, and $L_{g_1}L_{g_2}=L_{g_1g_2}$.

For a bounded complex-linear functional, write
$\|m\|:=\sup\{|m(f)|:\|f\|_\infty\le1\}$ for its operator norm.

A **mean** on $L^\infty(G)$ is a complex-linear functional
$m:L^\infty(G)\to\mathbb C$ such that $m(f)\ge0$ whenever $f\ge0$ and
$m(1_G)=1$, where $1_G$ is the class of the constant-one function. It is
**left invariant** if $m(L_gf)=m(f)$ for every $g\in G$ and
$f\in L^\infty(G)$. Every mean has operator norm one and satisfies
$$|m(f)|\le m(|f|)\le\|f\|_\infty.$$
Equivalently, a mean is a positive complex-linear functional of norm one.
items.strategy: Left translation maps Borel functions to Borel functions. If two representatives agree off a null set, their translates agree off its left translate, which is null; and each superlevel set of |L_g f| is the left translate of the corresponding superlevel set of |f|. Thus L_g is well defined and isometric, with the stated group law. For a positive complex-linear m, write each real-valued class u as u_+-u_- to see m(u) is real. For f with m(f) nonzero, choose alpha=conjugate(m(f))/|m(f)|; then m(Re(alpha f))=|m(f)| and Re(alpha f)<=|f|, so |m(f)|<=m(|f|). The essential-supremum definition gives |f|<=(||f||infinity+epsilon)1 almost everywhere; positivity yields m(|f|)<=(||f||infinity+epsilon)m(1). Let epsilon decrease to zero. Since ||1||infinity=1, taking the unit-ball supremum gives ||m||=m(1), so positive norm-one functionals are exactly means. No choice is used.

items.title: Amenable locally compact group
items.statement:
A locally compact Hausdorff group $G$ is **amenable** if there exists a
left-invariant mean $m$ on $L^\infty(G)$, using the fixed left Haar measure
and the translation action from
[[def-left-invariant-mean-on-l-infinity-of-a-locally-compact-group]]. Thus
$m$ is a positive complex-linear functional with $m(1_G)=1$ and
$m(L_gf)=m(f)$ for every $g\in G$ and $f\in L^\infty(G)$.

This definition imposes no countability, discreteness, compactness, or
unimodularity assumption. It does not depend on the normalization of Haar
measure: replacing $\mu$ by $c\mu$ for $c>0$ preserves exactly the same null
sets, so it gives the same almost-everywhere classes and essential-supremum
norm on $L^\infty(G)$. The mean and its left-invariance condition are therefore
unchanged.
items.strategy: Definition item. Normalization independence follows because replacing Haar measure by $c\mu$ for $c>0$ preserves exactly the same null sets; the almost-everywhere classes and essential-supremum norm on $L^\infty(G)$ are unchanged. Thus positivity, normalization, and left invariance of a mean are unchanged. No choice principle is used. Examples and existence results are treated later on this page.

items.title: Reiter's condition (P1)
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar measure
$\mu$, and put
$$\mathcal P:=\{f\in L^1(G):f\ge0,\ \|f\|_1=1\},$$
where $f\ge0$ means that the class has a real-valued representative that is
nonnegative almost everywhere. For $g\in G$ define
$(L_gf)(x):=f(g^{-1}x)$ on almost-everywhere classes. For compact
$Q\subseteq G$ and $f\in\mathcal P$, set
$$\Delta_Q(f):=\sup\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{\|L_gf-f\|_1:g\in Q\}\bigr).$$
Then $0\le\Delta_Q(f)\le2$, and $\Delta_\varnothing(f)=0$. The group $G$
satisfies **Reiter's condition (P1)** if for every compact $Q\subseteq G$
and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $f\in\mathcal P$ with
$\Delta_Q(f)\le\varepsilon$.

Equivalently, there is a net $(f_i)_{i\in I}$ in $\mathcal P$ with its
inherited $L^1$-norm topology such that for
every compact $Q$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ some $i_0\in I$ satisfies
$\Delta_Q(f_i)\le\varepsilon$ for all $i\succeq i_0$; this is uniform
convergence to zero on compact subsets. The set $\mathcal P$ is convex and
$L_g\mathcal P=\mathcal P$ for every $g\in G$. Only left translates are
used, the measure $\mu$ is fixed, and no compactness assumption on $G$ is
made.
items.strategy: For each left translation, the map x -> g^{-1}x is Borel and preserves Haar measure, so composition is well-defined on L1 classes, preserves nonnegativity and L1 norm, and its inverse is L_{g^{-1}}. Linearity of the integral proves convexity of P. The net equivalence uses the directed preorder of all witness triples (Q,epsilon,f), ordered by test-set inclusion and decreasing epsilon; every pair has a common upper witness by applying the condition to the union compact set and minimum tolerance. Each index contains its own witness, so no global choice is used.

items.title: Left Følner nets for locally compact groups
items.statement:
Fix a left Haar measure $\mu$ on a locally compact Hausdorff group $G$. For
a Borel set $F\subseteq G$ with $0<\mu(F)<\infty$ and a compact set
$Q\subseteq G$, put
$$\Delta_Q(F):=\sup\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{\mu(gF\mathbin\triangle F)/\mu(F):g\in Q\}\bigr).$$
The value is $0$ when $Q=\varnothing$. The group $G$ satisfies the **left
Følner condition** if for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every
$\varepsilon>0$ there is such a set $F$ with $\Delta_Q(F)\le\varepsilon$.

A **left Følner net** is a net $(F_i)_{i\in I}$ of Borel sets with
$0<\mu(F_i)<\infty$ such that for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every
$\varepsilon>0$ there is $i_0\in I$ for which
$\Delta_Q(F_i)\le\varepsilon$ whenever $i\succeq i_0$. This is uniform
convergence to zero on compact subsets. The left Følner condition holds if
and only if a left Følner net exists. In the single-set condition it is
equivalent to test only compact sets containing the identity. Only left
translates $gF$ occur.
items.strategy: The ratio is finite and at most two by left invariance and subadditivity, and including zero defines the empty-test value. A compact test Q can be enlarged to Q union {e}. A net gives a witness for each fixed (Q,epsilon). Conversely, index by all triples (Q,epsilon,F) in which F is a witness, ordered by inclusion of Q and decreasing epsilon. This is a directed preorder: for any two indices the union test set and the smaller positive tolerance have a witness by the assumed condition. The third coordinate gives a net satisfying the compact-uniform estimates. Because witnesses are themselves indices, no simultaneous choice function or Choice principle is needed.

items.title: Left-uniformly continuous bounded functions (UCB)
items.statement:
Let $B_b(G;\mathbb C)$ be the actual bounded complex-valued functions on a
locally compact Hausdorff group $G$, with
$\|\varphi\|_{\sup}:=\sup_{y\in G}|\varphi(y)|$. For $x\in G$ set
$(L_x\varphi)(y):=\varphi(x^{-1}y)$. Define
$$\mathrm{UCB}(G):=\{\varphi\in B_b(G;\mathbb C):\|L_x\varphi-\varphi\|_{\sup}\longrightarrow0\text{ as }x\longrightarrow e\}.$$
These are actual functions, not chosen representatives of equivalence
classes. They are continuous and form a closed translation-invariant subspace
of $B_b(G;\mathbb C)$. The left translation action
$G\times\mathrm{UCB}(G)\to\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ is jointly continuous in the
sup-norm topology. For any fixed left Haar measure $\mu$, the class map
$\varphi\mapsto[\varphi]$ embeds $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ isometrically into the
complex $L^\infty(G,\mu)$ space. In particular, a UCB function that vanishes
$\mu$-almost everywhere vanishes everywhere.
items.strategy: UCB consists of actual bounded functions whose left-translation orbit is continuous at the identity in the sup norm. Pointwise continuity follows by evaluating the translate at a fixed point. Linearity follows from the norm estimates; closedness follows from uniform limits. The group law and continuity of conjugation give translation invariance, and the estimate ||L_x phi-L_x0 phi0||sup <= ||phi-phi0||sup+||L_(x0^-1 x)phi0-phi0||sup gives joint continuity. For each continuous bounded phi, every strict sublevel below sup|phi| has a nonempty open superlevel set; full Haar support makes its measure positive. Hence sup norm equals essential-supremum norm, so the class map into complex L-infinity is an isometric injection. All of these arguments are choice-free.

items.title: Every locally compact Hausdorff group has an open sigma-compact subgroup
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff topological group and let $K$ be a
compact neighbourhood of its identity $e$. Set $U:=KK^{-1}$ and, for
$n\in\mathbb N$, let $U^n$ be the set of products of $n$ elements of $U$, with
$U^0:=\{e\}$. Then $H:=\bigcup_{n\in\mathbb N}U^n$ is an open subgroup of $G$
and a countable union of compact subsets. Here a topological space is
**sigma-compact** when it is a countable union of compact subsets. In
particular, every locally compact Hausdorff group has an open sigma-compact
subgroup. No axiom of choice is used.
items.strategy: Given a compact neighborhood K of e, form U=KK^{-1}. Inversion and multiplication are continuous, so U is compact; e in K implies K subset U, and the group inverse law makes U symmetric. The union H of finite powers of U is a subgroup. Induction, finite-product compactness and continuity of multiplication show each power is compact, hence H is sigma-compact. An open neighborhood V of e contained in K lies in H; H is the union of the open left translates hV, so it is open. The argument is choice-free; the finite-product compactness supplier uses only finite choice in ZF.

items.title: Finite Haar mass, compact detection, and integrable pairings
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G$ be an arbitrary locally compact Hausdorff group with its fixed left Haar measure $\mu$ under [[def-left-haar-integral-and-left-haar-measure]], and let $A\subseteq G$ be Borel. The following are equivalent:

1. $A$ contains a Borel $B$ with $0<\mu(B)<\infty$.
2. Some compact $K\subseteq G$ has $\mu(A\cap K)>0$.
3. Some nonnegative $f\in L^1(G)$ has $\int_A f\,d\mu>0$.

Call $A$ **locally null** when $\mu(A\cap K)=0$ for every compact $K$. Thus a locally null Borel set is annihilated by every $L^1$ pairing, even though it need not be globally $\mu$-null. Positive global Haar measure alone does not imply these equivalent conditions; the counterexample in Remarks retains the original scaffold's obstruction. No sigma-compactness, semifiniteness or locally-null quotient convention is assumed.
items.strategy: Prove the corrected arbitrary-LCH claim locally, keeping global-null Haar conventions and retaining original counterexamples in Remarks. Finite positive mass is detected by compact intersections and by L1 threshold sets; derive finite-measure regularity from outer regularity and open inner approximation.

items.title: Probability-density averages and locally detectable upper essential values
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G$ be an arbitrary LCH group with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$, and put $\mathcal P=\{f\in L^1(G):f\ge0,\ \|f\|_1=1\}$. For a real global-$L^\infty$ class $h$, choose a bounded Borel representative and define its **locally detectable upper essential value** by
$$\beta(h):=\inf\{t\in\mathbb R:\mu(K\cap\{h>t\})=0\text{ for every compact }K\subseteq G\}.$$
This is a finite real number independent of that representative, and
$$\sup_{f\in\mathcal P}\int_Gfh\,d\mu=\beta(h).$$
For complex $h\in L^\infty(G)$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb C$, the exact support-function formula is
$$\sup_{f\in\mathcal P}\operatorname{Re}\left(\alpha\int_Gfh\,d\mu\right)=\beta(\operatorname{Re}(\alpha h)).$$
For every real bounded continuous $h$, one has $\beta(h)=\sup_{x\in G}h(x)$. All $L^\infty$ classes here retain the global-null convention of [[def-complex-haar-l-infinity-space]]; locally null functions are not identified with zero. The original global-norm formula and its naive global-essential-upper-value repair fail as explained in Remarks.
items.strategy: Prove the corrected arbitrary-LCH claim locally, keeping global-null Haar conventions and retaining original counterexamples in Remarks. Use locally detectable superlevels for lower bounds and nonnegative Cc approximants for upper bounds; complex support values are signed real parts, and continuous values equal sup_G.

items.title: L1 convolution smooths bounded functions into UCB
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar
measure $\mu$, and set $L_gf(x):=f(g^{-1}x)$. For $f,b\in L^1(G)$ and
$\varphi\in L^\infty(G)$, define
$$
(f*\varphi)(x):=\int_G f(y)\varphi(y^{-1}x)\,d\mu(y)\qquad(x\in G).
$$
This formula defines an actual bounded continuous function independent of the
representatives, with
$$\|f*\varphi\|_{\sup}\le\|f\|_1\|\varphi\|_\infty.$$
It belongs to $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ and satisfies
$$\|L_g(f*\varphi)-f*\varphi\|_{\sup}\le\|L_gf-f\|_1\|\varphi\|_\infty$$
for every $g\in G$, as well as $L_g(f*\varphi)=(L_gf)*\varphi$. The operation
is bilinear in $f$ and $\varphi$. With the extended $L^1$ convolution of
[[def-convolution-on-cc-and-l1-of-a-group]], it also satisfies
$$ (f*b)*\varphi=f*(b*\varphi)\qquad(f,b\in L^1(G)). $$
items.strategy: Define the pointwise L1-L-infinity convolution using Borel representatives and prove representative independence from inversion and left invariance. Estimate its sup norm and left-translation defect directly. For associativity with a Borel bounded function, first use compactly supported L1 factors and a finite Borel partition to approximate the continuous kernel b(y^{-1}z) uniformly on compact parameter sets; Fubini then applies to finite sums of product-measurable functions on finite-measure compact restrictions. Extend to arbitrary L1 factors by Cc density and the convolution and smoothing norm bounds. This proves the actual-function UCB claim and the associativity identity without global sigma-finiteness or product-Borel assumptions.

items.title: A UCB-invariant mean yields a topological invariant mean
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar
measure $\mu$, and let $m$ be a left-invariant mean on the actual-function
space $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$ of [[def-left-uniformly-continuous-bounded-functions-on-a-locally-compact-group]]. Thus $m$ is a positive complex-linear functional with $m(1_G)=1$ and $m(L_g\psi)=m(\psi)$ for every $g\in G$ and $\psi\in\mathrm{UCB}(G)$. Fix $f_0\in\mathcal P$ for $\mathcal P$ of [[def-reiter-condition-p1]], and define
$$\widetilde m(\varphi):=m(f_0*\varphi)\qquad(\varphi\in L^\infty(G)),$$
where $*$ is the pointwise $L^1$-to-$L^\infty$ smoothing of
[[lem-l1-convolution-with-an-l-infinity-function-is-left-uniformly-continuous]].
Then $\widetilde m$ is a mean on $L^\infty(G)$ and is topologically invariant:
$$\widetilde m(f*\varphi)=\widetilde m(\varphi)\qquad(f\in\mathcal P,\ \varphi\in L^\infty(G)).$$
items.strategy: First prove the integration mean has norm one. Use a finite Borel partition of a compact set to approximate the continuous UCB translation orbit uniformly; the L1 tail is small by Cc density. This gives m(f*psi)=m(psi) for f in P and psi in UCB without Bochner measurability. Apply this identity to psi=e_U*phi and use the right-L1 approximate-identity estimate ||(f*e_U)*phi-f*phi||sup <= ||f*e_U-f||1 ||phi||infinity to show m(f*phi) is independent of f in P. Prove P is closed under L1 convolution by nonnegative Cc approximations, compact-support Fubini, continuity of extended convolution, and closedness of the nonnegative cone. Then m-tilde(phi)=m(f0*phi) is a mean, and associativity plus P closure make it topologically invariant. Topological invariance follows from associativity, probability-convolution closure and kernel independence: m((f0*f)*phi)=m(f0*phi). Every argument of the UCB mean is smoothed; the mean is never evaluated on an arbitrary unsmoothed L-infinity input.

items.title: Probability-density approximation of continuous tests and topological means
items.statement:
Assume AC ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $G$ be an arbitrary LCH group with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$, let $\mathcal P=\{f\in L^1(G):f\ge0,\ \|f\|_1=1\}$ and let $M$ be the means on the global-null $L^\infty(G)$ of [[def-left-invariant-mean-on-l-infinity-of-a-locally-compact-group]]. Then:

1. Every $m\in M$, finite list of bounded continuous functions $\psi_1,\ldots,\psi_k$ and $\varepsilon>0$ admit $f\in\mathcal P\cap C_c(G)$ with $|\int f\psi_j\,d\mu-m([\psi_j])|<\varepsilon$ for all $j$.
2. If $m$ is **topologically invariant**, meaning $m(p*\varphi)=m(\varphi)$ for every $p\in\mathcal P$ and $\varphi\in L^\infty(G)$ using the smoothing of [[lem-l1-convolution-with-an-l-infinity-function-is-left-uniformly-continuous]], then $m$ is in the weak-star closure of $\mathcal P$: every finite list of global $L^\infty$ classes can be approximated simultaneously by their probability-density integrals.

Here $\mathcal P$ embeds into $L^\infty(G)^*$ by integration. Full weak-star density in ALL means is false under the existing Haar/global-null conventions; the original counterexample remains in Remarks. No countability or semifiniteness of $G$ is imposed.

items.title: A topological invariant mean yields norm-approximately invariant densities
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar
measure $\mu$, and let $\widetilde m$ be a topological invariant mean on
$L^\infty(G)$: a positive complex-linear functional with
$\widetilde m(1_G)=1$ and
$\widetilde m(f*\varphi)=\widetilde m(\varphi)$ for every
$f\in\mathcal P$ and $\varphi\in L^\infty(G)$, where $\mathcal P$ is the
set of probability densities from [[def-reiter-condition-p1]]. The product
$f*\varphi$ is the $L^1$–$L^\infty$ smoothing of
[[lem-l1-convolution-with-an-l-infinity-function-is-left-uniformly-continuous]];
products of two $L^1$ classes below use the extended convolution of
[[def-convolution-on-cc-and-l1-of-a-group]].
Then there is a net $(g_j)\subseteq\mathcal P$ such that
$\lVert f*g_j-g_j\rVert_1\to0$ for every $f\in\mathcal P$. The convergence
is uniform on norm-compact subsets of $\mathcal P$: for every norm-compact
$C\subseteq\mathcal P$ and every $\delta>0$ there is $j_0$ such that
$\sup_{f\in C}\lVert f*g_j-g_j\rVert_1<\delta$ whenever $j\succeq j_0$.
items.strategy: Prove finite-test density of probability densities against bounded continuous functions by placing the mean-value tuple in the closed convex hull of point values, using strict separation, then approximating point evaluations by normalized indicators of relatively compact open neighborhoods. Build a witness-indexed net approximating the mean on all bounded continuous tests. Prove every bounded complex functional on L1 is represented by a bounded Borel function: restrict to each clopen sigma-compact coset, use sigma-finite real L1 duality for real and imaginary parts, approximate local densities on compact exhaustions by Cc functions, clip them uniformly, glue continuous approximants across the clopen cosets, take a Borel pointwise limit, and extend the pairing from global Cc by density; do not take an uncountable union of null sets. Discharge zero inputs before compact-support modular suprema. Establish the adjoint convolution pairing first for Cc inputs and continuous tests by compact Radon integration, extend bounded Borel tests by Cc L1 approximation on the compact product support and modular bounds, then extend L1 inputs by norm continuity. Smooth the continuous-test net with one fixed probability density p via g_i=p^sharp*b_i; the adjoint identity and topological invariance give weak-star convergence of g_i to the given mean on all L-infinity tests. Hence each convolution defect tends weakly to zero in L1 by the full dual representation. Apply Mazur to finite products for finite-test norm approximation, index witnesses by finite tests and tolerances, and use a finite norm net to obtain uniformity on norm-compact subsets.

items.title: An invariant mean produces a Reiter net
items.statement: Assume AC. Suppose $G$ admits a left-invariant mean on $\mathrm{UCB}(G)$; this holds in particular when $G$ is amenable in the sense of [[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]. Then $G$ satisfies Reiter's condition (P1) ([[def-reiter-condition-p1]]). Consequently every amenable locally compact group satisfies (P1).
items.strategy: First convert a left-invariant mean on actual UCB(G) to a topological invariant mean and use the preceding norm-approximation result to obtain a probability-density net uniform on norm-compact subsets of P. For a compact Q, adjoin e, fix f in P, and use strong continuity to make {L_x f : x in Q union {e}} a compact subset of P. Prove locally that extended L1 convolution is left-equivariant, first by the Cc formula and left Haar substitution, then by Cc density and the L1 convolution bound. Choose one net index that controls the whole orbit, set g=f*g_j, and use convolution closure of P to obtain the compact Reiter estimate. An amenable L-infinity mean restricts through the UCB class embedding, giving the final consequence.

items.title: A Reiter net has an invariant-mean cluster point
items.statement:
Assume the ultrafilter lemma. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with
fixed left Haar measure $\mu$, and let $(f_i)_{i\in I}$ be a Reiter net on $G$
as in [[def-reiter-condition-p1]]. Define
$$\lambda_{f_i}(\varphi):=\int_G f_i\varphi\,d\mu\qquad(\varphi\in L^\infty(G)).$$
Then $(\lambda_{f_i})$ has a weak-star cluster point $m$ in
$L^\infty(G)^*$. Every such cluster point is a left-invariant mean on
$L^\infty(G)$, so Reiter's condition (P1) implies that $G$ is amenable
([[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]).
items.strategy: For each Reiter density define the integration functional on complex L-infinity. Essential bounds make each pairing integrable and give norm at most one. Banach–Alaoglu under the ultrafilter lemma puts the net in a weak-star compact dual ball, so it has a cluster point and each cluster point is the limit of a subnet. Positivity and evaluation at 1 pass to subnet limits. For any fixed g and phi, left-Haar substitution gives lambda_f(L_g phi)=lambda_{L_(g^{-1)}f}(phi); the Reiter estimate on {g^{-1}} makes the defect tend to zero, and weak-star convergence along the subnet gives invariance. The equivalent net formulation of P1 then yields amenability.

items.title: Amenability is equivalent to Reiter's condition (P1)
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group. Then $G$ is amenable ([[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]) if and only if $G$ satisfies Reiter's condition (P1) ([[def-reiter-condition-p1]]): for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is $f\in L^1(G)$ with $f\ge0$, $\lVert f\rVert_1=1$ and $\Delta_Q(f)\le\varepsilon$, with $\Delta_Q$ as defined in
[[def-reiter-condition-p1]] (including $\Delta_\varnothing(f)=0$). The equivalence is proved through invariant means on $L^\infty(G)$, so it is stated for a fixed left Haar measure but does not depend on its normalization.
items.strategy: Assume AC. If G is amenable, restrict its L-infinity mean through the UCB class embedding to obtain a left-invariant mean on actual UCB(G); the invariant-mean-to-Reiter supplier gives (P1). Conversely, (P1) gives a Reiter net by its net formulation; AC supplies the ultrafilter lemma, and the Reiter-net cluster-point supplier gives a left-invariant mean on L-infinity(G). This is amenability. The all-means weak-star-density route from the literature is not used; both directions use the local bridge items. Rescaling Haar measure by c>0 identifies the probability densities via f↦c^{-1}f and preserves every translation defect, while amenability is normalization independent.

items.title: Følner nets give Reiter nets
items.statement:
Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar measure
$\mu$, and let $F\subseteq G$ be Borel with $0<\mu(F)<\infty$. The class
$$f_F:=\mu(F)^{-1}\mathbf 1_F\in L^1(G)$$
belongs to $\mathcal P$ from [[def-reiter-condition-p1]], and for every
$x\in G$,
$$\|L_xf_F-f_F\|_1=\frac{\mu(xF\mathbin\triangle F)}{\mu(F)}.$$
Consequently, every left Følner net $(F_i)$ gives a Reiter net
$(f_{F_i})$. In particular, the left Følner condition implies Reiter's
condition (P1).
items.strategy: For a Borel set F of positive finite Haar measure, the indicator is a nonnegative simple function, so its L1 norm is its measure and f_F=mu(F)^(-1)1_F belongs to P. The left translate of 1_F is 1_(xF); its difference from 1_F has modulus 1 exactly on xF symmetric-difference F, giving the exact norm ratio by the integral of a simple indicator. The same estimates give the Reiter net and single-set condition, with no global choice.

items.title: The layer-cake identity for integrable functions
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice. Let $(X,\mathcal A,\mu)$ be any measure
space, and let $f,g\in L^1(X)$ be nonnegative integrable functions with fixed
pointwise nonnegative measurable representatives. For $t>0$ put
$E_t:=\{x\in X:f(x)\ge t\}$ and $E'_t:=\{x\in X:g(x)\ge t\}$, and let $dt$
denote Lebesgue measure on the level parameter. Then
$$\lVert f-g\rVert_1=\int_0^\infty\mu(E_t\mathbin\triangle E'_t)\,dt,$$
and in particular
$$\lVert f\rVert_1=\int_0^\infty\mu(E_t)\,dt.$$
No $\sigma$-finiteness of $\mu$ is required: both integrands are supported on
$S:=\{x:f(x)+g(x)>0\}$, which is $\sigma$-finite.
items.strategy: Assume AC_omega only to use the library Lebesgue measure on R as a countably additive sigma-finite measure. Set h=f+g and S={h>0}; the Chebyshev-Markov inequality shows S is a countable union of finite-measure level sets, so the restricted measure on S is sigma-finite and f=g=0 outside S. For each f, the product set {(x,t):x in S, 0<t<=f(x)} is measurable: it is the countable intersection over m>=1 of the countable unions over positive rationals q of (S intersect {f>q}) times (0,q+1/m]. Rationals are countable and dense. Its symmetric difference with the corresponding set for g has sections E_t triangle E'_t and, at each x, a t-section of Lebesgue measure |f(x)-g(x)|. Tonelli on the sigma-finite product S times R then gives the identity. Setting g=0 gives the norm formula. The source proofs leave the support sigma-finiteness reduction implicit; this strategy supplies it explicitly. No full AC or DC.

items.title: Reiter functions can be cut down to Følner sets
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally
compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$, let $Q\subseteq G$
be compact with $\mu(Q)>0$, let $\varepsilon>0$, and let $f\in L^1(G)$ satisfy
$f\ge0$, $\lVert f\rVert_1=1$ and
$$\sup_{x\in Q^2}\lVert L_xf-f\rVert_1\le\frac{\varepsilon\mu(Q)}{2\mu(Q^2)},$$
where $Q^2:=\{xy:x,y\in Q\}$. Then there is a Borel set $U\subseteq G$ with
$0<\mu(U)<\infty$ and
$$\sup_{x\in Q}\frac{\mu(xU\mathbin\triangle U)}{\mu(U)}\le2\varepsilon.$$
Consequently Reiter's condition (P1) implies the left Følner condition: for
every compact $Q$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ a Borel set $U$ with
$0<\mu(U)<\infty$ and
$$\sup_{x\in Q}\frac{\mu(xU\mathbin\triangle U)}{\mu(U)}\le2\varepsilon$$
exists.
The supremum over an empty compact test set in the consequent is taken to be $0$.
items.strategy: Average the compact L1 orbit of the single given density using finite Borel partitions, then parity-symmetrize h=(f+g)/2 to obtain Q defect≤3δ/2 and Q² defect≤2δ. For each finite-positive U integrate d_x(U)≤d_a(U)+d_xa(U) over a∈Q using xQ⊂Q², yielding uniform Q control by C_Q(U)+C_Q²(U). Strict-superlevel dyadic right-step continuity gives product measurability without global product-Borel assumptions. Layercake/Tonelli and weighted selection give one level with boundary≤δ(3/2+2r)≤7ε/4<2ε; δ=0 is included. For P1, enlarge an arbitrary target by a compact identity neighborhood and request the necessary fresh data. The source e∈Q route is documented but not used.

items.title: The Følner criterion for locally compact groups
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$. Then $G$ is amenable ([[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]) if and only if it satisfies the left Følner condition ([[def-left-folner-net-for-a-locally-compact-group]]): for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a Borel set $F\subseteq G$ with $0<\mu(F)<\infty$ and $\Delta_Q(F)\le\varepsilon$. Equivalently, $G$ admits a left Følner net. Borel sets suffice for $F$.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Amenability implies Reiter (P1) by the preceding equivalence theorem. For the Reiter-to-Følner direction, enlarge an arbitrary compact target Q to P=Q union C, where C is a compact identity neighbourhood, and let K=P^2. Then P has finite positive Haar measure, contains e, and K is compact. Choose f in the Reiter probabilities with sup_{x in K} ||L_x f-f||_1 <= eta mu(P)/(4 mu(K)), where eta=epsilon/2. For E_t={f>=t}, layer cake and Tonelli on K times (0,infinity), with product measurability proved by increasing dyadic levels, give an average normalized boundary r(t) whose mu(E_t)-weighted integral is at most eta mu(P)/4. Since integral mu(E_t) dt=1, choose t with 0<mu(E_t)<infinity and r(t)<eta mu(P)/2. The good set A={x in K: mu(xE_t triangle E_t)/mu(E_t)<=eta} then has complement of measure <mu(P)/2. For each x in P, xP is contained in xK intersect K and has measure mu(P), so xA intersect A has positive measure. Thus x=a_1 a_2^{-1} for a_1,a_2 in A; the symmetric-difference triangle inequality and left invariance give mu(xE_t triangle E_t)<=2 eta mu(E_t)=epsilon mu(E_t). The set E_t is the required Borel Følner witness. Conversely, normalized indicators turn Følner sets into Reiter probabilities, and Reiter (P1) implies amenability. This proves the full LCH criterion without using the separate, independently proved stronger cutdown lemma.

items.title: Folner sequences for second countable compactly generated groups
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be an amenable second countable compactly generated locally compact Hausdorff group ([[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]], [[def-locally-compact-space]], [[def-hausdorff-space]]) with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$ ([[def-left-haar-integral-and-left-haar-measure]]), and let $S\subseteq G$ be a compact generating set ([[def-compact-space]], [[def-topological-group]]) with $S=S^{-1}$ containing $e$ and a nonempty open set. Then there is a sequence $(F_n)_{n\ge0}$ of Borel sets with $0<\mu(F_n)<\infty$ such that for every compact $Q\subseteq G$
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\Delta_Q(F_n)=0,\qquad\Delta_Q(F):=\sup\bigl(\{0\}\cup\{\mu(xF\mathbin\triangle F)/\mu(F):x\in Q\}\bigr).$$
Thus $\Delta_\varnothing(F)=0$.
Such a sequence is a **Følner sequence** for $G$. Conversely, a locally compact Hausdorff group with such a sequence satisfies the left Følner condition ([[def-left-folner-net-for-a-locally-compact-group]]) and hence is amenable, so for such a group amenability is equivalent to the existence of a Følner sequence. Only compact generation, not second countability, is used by the construction.
items.strategy: Repaired scaffold route. Put $K_n:=S^n$: the n-fold multiplication map is continuous on the compact product $S\times\cdots\times S$, so $K_n$ is compact and $K_n\subseteq K_{n+1}$. From the nonempty open $U\subseteq S=S^{-1}$ the open set $W=U\cdot U^{-1}$ contains $e$ and lies in $S^2$, so $S^m\subseteq\operatorname{int}(S^{m+2})$ for every $m$; the open sets $\operatorname{int}(K_{2n})$ increase and cover $G$, so every compact $Q$ lies in $K_n$ for all large $n$. Apply the Folner criterion ([[thm-folner-criterion-for-locally-compact-groups]]) to the compact set $K_{n+1}$ at tolerance $1/(n+1)$ and select one witness $F_n$ per $n\ge0$ using ACω; then $\Delta_Q(F_n)\le\Delta_{K_{n+1}}(F_n)\le1/(n+1)\to0$, so $(F_n)$ is a Folner sequence. Conversely a Folner sequence gives the left Folner condition and hence amenability by the criterion. The scaffold statement's hypothesis list omitted amenability, which is necessary: the second countable compactly generated group $F_2$ is not amenable and has no Folner sequence. The amenability hypothesis is restored from the source's Remark G.5.3 (amenability is equivalent to the existence of a Folner sequence for compactly generated G); only compact generation, not second countability, enters the construction.

items.title: The Hulanicki–Reiter weak containment criterion for amenability
items.statement: Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with fixed left Haar measure $\mu$. Let $1_G$ be the trivial unitary representation on $\mathbb C$ with its standard inner product, given by $1_G(g)z=z$, and let $\lambda_G$ be the left regular representation on $L^2(G)$ ([[def-left-and-right-regular-unitary-representations]], [[thm-regular-representations-are-unitary-and-strongly-continuous]]). Then $G$ is amenable ([[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]) if and only if $1_G\prec\lambda_G$ ([[def-weak-containment-of-unitary-representations]]). Equivalently, $G$ is amenable if and only if $\lambda_G$ almost has invariant unit vectors: for every compact $Q\subseteq G$ and every $\varepsilon>0$ there is a unit vector $\xi\in L^2(G)$ with $\sup_{x\in Q}\lVert\lambda_G(x)\xi-\xi\rVert_2<\varepsilon$.
items.strategy: Assume AC. Amenability yields Reiter (P1). For any compact Q and epsilon, choose a probability density f with defect at most epsilon^2/2 and set g=sqrt(f); the scalar square-root estimate gives an almost-invariant unit vector for lambda_G. If lambda_G has almost-invariant unit vectors, their normalized coefficients approximate each constant coefficient of 1_G, so 1_G is weakly contained in lambda_G. Conversely 1_G weakly contained in lambda_G gives almost-invariant unit vectors by the local lemma. For such a unit vector xi, f=|xi|^2 is a Reiter probability: the pointwise reverse-triangle bound on squared moduli, Cauchy-Schwarz, and unitarity give ||L_x f-f||_1<=2||lambda_G(x)xi-xi||_2. Reiter (P1) then gives amenability; the weak-containment lemma supplies the equivalent vector formulation.

items.title: The Markov-Kakutani fixed point theorem for abelian affine actions
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $G$ be an abelian topological group, and let
$X$ be a nonempty compact convex subset of a Hausdorff locally convex real or
complex topological vector space $V$. Suppose $G$ acts continuously on $X$;
write $gx$ for the action, with $e x=x$ and $(gh)x=g(hx)$. Each action map is
affine in the finite-combination sense: for $x_0,\dots,x_n\in X$ and real
$t_i\ge0$ with $\sum_{i=0}^n t_i=1$,
$$g\left(\sum_{i=0}^n t_i x_i\right)=\sum_{i=0}^n t_i(gx_i).$$
Then there exists $x_0\in X$ with $gx_0=x_0$ for every $g\in G$.
items.strategy: Assume AC only to obtain the real Hahn-Banach extension principle by the Zorn-based dominated-extension theorem; the averages, compact finite-intersection argument, and estimates use no choice. For each $g$ and $n\ge0$, form the affine continuous averaging map $A_n(g)x=(n+1)^{-1}\sum_{i=0}^n g^ix$. Their pairwise commutation follows by expanding the finite double averages and using that $G$ is abelian. Let $\Gamma$ be the monoid they generate, including the identity. The nonempty compact closed images $\gamma(X)$ have the finite intersection property, so choose $x_0$ in their intersection. Fix $g$ and suppose $v=x_0-gx_0\ne0$. Hahn-Banach dual separation supplies a continuous linear functional whose real part $\psi$ is nonzero on $v$; compactness bounds $|\psi|$ on $X$ by $C$. For each $n$, membership $x_0\in A_n(g)(X)$ and telescoping give $|\psi(v)|\le2C/(n+1)$. The reciprocal Archimedean property forces $\psi(v)=0$, contradiction. Thus each $g$ fixes $x_0$.

items.title: The fixed point property implies amenability
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group with the fixed point
property: every continuous affine action of $G$ on a nonempty compact convex
subset of a Hausdorff locally convex topological vector space has a fixed point. Then
$G$ is amenable ([[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]).
items.strategy: Let X=UCB(G) and put E=X* with the weak-star topology. Construct M, the set of positive complex-linear unital functionals on X. Show M is nonempty, convex, weak-star closed and contained in the dual unit ball by proving every mean has norm at most one. The weak-star topology makes E a Hausdorff locally convex topological vector space, since distinct functionals are separated by evaluations. AC implies the ultrafilter lemma, so Banach–Alaoglu makes the dual ball compact and then M compact. Define (g·m)(psi)=m(L_{g^{-1}}psi); verify this is an affine action on M and prove joint continuity using norm continuity of UCB translation orbits and weak-star evaluations. Apply the fixed point property to obtain a left-invariant UCB mean. Apply the UCB-to-Reiter lemma and the Reiter-net cluster-point lemma; AC supplies the ultrafilter lemma required by both compactness steps, yielding an invariant mean on L-infinity and amenability.

items.title: Compact and locally compact abelian groups are amenable
items.statement:
Assume AC. (1) Every compact locally compact Hausdorff group is amenable.
(2) Every locally compact Hausdorff abelian group is amenable. No countability,
metrizability or unimodularity hypothesis is imposed.
items.strategy: (1) Under AC choose a left Haar measure ν on K; since K is nonempty open and compact, Haar positivity and compact finiteness give 0<ν(K)<∞. Rescale μ=ν/ν(K), so μ is a normalized left Haar probability. For every φ∈L∞(K,μ;C), essential boundedness and μ(K)=1 imply φ∈L1; almost-everywhere equality preserves the integral, so m(φ)=∫K φ dμ is well-defined. Linearity, positivity, the estimate |m(φ)|≤||φ||∞ and m(1K)=1 make m a mean. Each left translation T_g(x)=g^-1x is Borel and measure-preserving; integral invariance gives m(L_gφ)=m(φ), so K is amenable. (2) Let G be LCH and abelian. The Hausdorff Markov–Kakutani theorem ([[lem-markov-kakutani-fixed-point-theorem-for-abelian-affine-actions]]) gives the fixed-point property for continuous affine actions on nonempty compact convex subsets of Hausdorff locally convex spaces. The fixed-point-property-to-amenability lemma ([[lem-a-group-with-the-fixed-point-property-is-amenable]]) then gives amenability.

items.title: Restriction of the regular representation to a closed subgroup
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group and let $H\leq G$ be
closed. Fix left Haar measures on $G$ and $H$. Then the restriction of the left
regular representation of $G$ to $H$ is weakly contained in the left regular
representation of $H$:
$$\lambda_G|_H\prec\lambda_H,$$
where weak containment means uniform approximation of each diagonal coefficient
on every compact subset of $H$ by finite sums of diagonal coefficients.
items.strategy: Fix f in C_c(G), let r and mu be the rho-function and Radon quotient measure, and set a_x(h)=[Delta_G((xh)^(-1))/r(xh)]^(1/2) f((xh)^(-1)). Its support is compact in H. The coefficient B(xH,k)=<R_H(k)a_x,a_x> is independent of the representative by left Haar invariance, is jointly continuous by compact-kernel integration, and vanishes outside the compact quotient image of supp(f)^(-1). Inversion and the Weil formula give <lambda_G(k)f,f>=integral_(G/H)B(q,k)dmu(q). For compact Q in H, joint continuity and compactness give a finite Borel partition of the compact support on which B(q,.) oscillates uniformly by less than delta; the weighted sum with vectors sqrt(mu(E_j))a_(x_j) approximates the integral within delta mu(T). The inversion intertwiner Jb(h)=Delta_H(h)^(-1/2)b(h^(-1)) carries these right-regular coefficients to left-regular coefficients. Finally approximate arbitrary xi in L2(G) by f in C_c(G); unitarity and Cauchy-Schwarz make the coefficient error uniform on Q. AC is explicit and no measurable section or direct integral is used.

It supplies the rho-function and Radon quotient measure and discharges the choice hypotheses of the Weil, quotient, kernel, inversion, regular-representation and C_c-density suppliers. The proof makes only finite choices when forming its partition and choosing quotient lifts; it uses no measurable section, direct integral, countability hypothesis, or stronger choice principle.

items.title: Amenability is stable under closed subgroups, quotients and extensions
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $G$ be a locally compact Hausdorff group. (i) If $G$ is
amenable, every closed subgroup $H\leq G$ is amenable. (ii) If $G$ is
amenable and $N\trianglelefteq G$ is closed normal, the Hausdorff quotient
$G/N$ is amenable. (iii) If $N\trianglelefteq G$ is closed normal and both
$N$ and $G/N$ are amenable, then $G$ is amenable.
items.strategy: For closed subgroups, restrict the coefficient approximations from the Hulanicki criterion and use the assigned restricted-regular-representation lemma plus transitivity. Prove first that a closed-normal quotient with quotient topology is a topological LCH group. For quotient inheritance, pull back actual UCB functions and restrict the L-infinity mean. For extensions, set phi_g(h)=phi(gh), prove the conjugation estimate placing phi_g in UCB(N), average it with an N-invariant mean, descend through the open quotient map, verify quotient UCB by the exact sup-defect equality, and use the UCB-to-Reiter and Reiter-to-amenability suppliers. No global section is chosen.

title: Amenability Reiter Nets and Folner Conditions — Examples

items.title: Følner sets in $\mathbb R^n$
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $n\ge1$, let $G=\mathbb R^n$ be the additive group with its
Euclidean topology, and let $\lambda_n$ be Lebesgue measure. Then $\lambda_n$
is a left Haar measure on $G$. For every compact $Q\subseteq\mathbb R^n$,
choose $R\ge0$ such that $Q\subseteq[-R,R]^n$, and for $t>0$ put
$C_t:=[-t,t]^n$. Then
$$\Delta_Q(C_t)=\sup\Bigl(\{0\}\cup\Bigl\{\frac{\lambda_n((x+C_t)\mathbin\triangle C_t)}{\lambda_n(C_t)}:x\in Q\Bigr\}\Bigr)\le2\bigl((1+R/t)^n-1\bigr)\xrightarrow[t\to\infty]{}0,$$
where $\Delta_Q$ is the left Følner defect of
[[def-left-folner-net-for-a-locally-compact-group]]. In particular
$(C_t)_{t>0}$ is a left Følner net, $G$ satisfies the left Følner condition,
and $\mathbb R^n$ is amenable by
[[thm-folner-criterion-for-locally-compact-groups]].
items.strategy: Under AC_omega, the Lebesgue measurable sets form a sigma-algebra, Lebesgue measure is complete and Radon, and translation invariance plus the box formula give positive finite measure to each C_t; hence it is left Haar. For compact Q obtain R>=0 by compactness implying Euclidean boundedness. For each x in Q, reduce the symmetric difference to twice one one-sided difference using equal finite measures; that one-sided difference lies in the expanded outer box minus C_t. Its measure gives exactly the displayed bound. The binomial theorem gives an explicit T(Q,epsilon) after which the ratio is at most epsilon, so the directed family t>0 is a left Folner net. Invoke the AC-dependent Folner criterion for amenability.

items.title: Compact groups have a constant Reiter net
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let $K$ be a compact locally compact Hausdorff group. Choose a left
Haar measure $\nu$ on $K$ and put $\mu:=\nu/\nu(K)$; the denominator is positive
and finite, so $\mu$ is a normalized Haar probability. Let
$f:=\mathbf 1_K\in L^1(K)$. Then
$f\ge0$, $\lVert f\rVert_1=1$, and $L_xf=f$ for every $x\in K$, because
$L_x\mathbf 1_K=\mathbf 1_{xK}=\mathbf 1_K$. Hence the constant net
$f_i:=f$ satisfies Reiter's condition (P1) exactly, with
$\Delta_Q(f)=0$ for every compact $Q\subseteq K$,
and $K$ is amenable by [[thm-amenability-is-equivalent-to-reiter-p1]]. This is
the strongest possible form of approximate invariance: the approximating
densities do not vary with the tolerance.
items.strategy: Under AC choose a left Haar measure on the compact group. Since the whole group is nonempty, open and compact, its Haar measure is finite and positive; rescaling by that value gives a normalized Haar probability. The density 1_K then has L1 norm one and is fixed exactly by every left translation, so the singleton constant net satisfies (P1) with zero defect on every compact test. Reiter equivalence gives amenability. The same normalized-Haar integral directly defines an invariant mean on complex L-infinity classes, explicitly checking the compact-group clause of the earlier compact/abelian amenability proposition.

references.locator: Appendix G.1, Example G.1.5 (printed p. 448), identifies normalized Haar probability as the invariant mean on C(K); Appendix G.3, Theorem G.3.1(iii) (printed pp. 452-453), states Reiter (P1). The item locally verifies the complex L-infinity mean on equivalence classes.

items.axiom_use: Assume AC. It is used through left Haar measure existence, normalization by the positive finite measure of the compact group, and the Reiter-to-amenability equivalence. The constant net and integral invariance calculation add no further choice or dependent-choice use.

items.title: The real affine group is amenable and nonunimodular
items.statement:
Assume AC. Let
$$G:=\{(a,b):a>0,\ b\in\mathbb R\}$$
with multiplication
$$(a,b)(a',b')=(aa',ab'+b)$$
and the topology inherited from $\mathbb R^2$. Then $G$ is a locally compact
Hausdorff topological group and is amenable. The measure
$$d\mu_L(a,b)=a^{-2}\,da\,db$$
is a left Haar measure for which the library's modular convention gives
$$\Delta_G(a,b)=a^{-1}.$$
In particular, $G$ is nonunimodular, so amenability does not imply
unimodularity.
items.strategy: Prove the fixed-point property directly: apply Markov–Kakutani to N=R and then to H=R_{>0} on the N-fixed compact convex set, and invoke the fixed-point-property-to-amenability result. Define the positive smooth density a^(-2)|da db|, prove it is nonzero Radon under AC_omega, compute the left-translation Jacobian to verify left Haar invariance, then compute the inverse-right-translation change-of-variables scalar to obtain Delta(a,b)=a^(-1) under the library convention.

items.title: The free group on two generators is not amenable
items.statement:
Let $F_2=\langle a,b\rangle$ be the free group on two generators with the
 discrete topology, and let $\mu$ be counting measure, a left Haar measure by
[[lem-counting-measure-on-a-discrete-group]]. Then $F_2$ is not amenable: there
is no left-invariant mean on $L^\infty(F_2,\mu)$ in the sense of
[[def-amenable-locally-compact-group]]. The direct proof below also establishes
the published discrete nonamenability claim [[thm-free-group-of-rank-two-is-nonamenable]].
items.strategy: Because the topology is discrete, $\mu$ is counting measure, every function on $F_2$ is $\mu$-measurable and the only $\mu$-null set is $\varnothing$; hence $L^\infty(F_2,\mu)=\ell^\infty(F_2)$ literally, and a left-invariant mean in the sense of [[def-left-invariant-mean-on-l-infinity-of-a-locally-compact-group]] is exactly a left-invariant mean on $\ell^\infty(F_2)$ in the discrete sense of [[def-left-invariant-mean-and-amenable-group]]. Suppose such an $m$ exists. For a subset $A\subseteq F_2$ write $m(A):=m(\mathbf 1_A)$. Let $A$ be the set of reduced words beginning with a nonzero power of $a$ (including the empty word convention is immaterial); every element of $F_2$ is either in $A$ or of the form $a w$ with $w\in A$ wait, more precisely $F_2=A\sqcup aA$: a reduced word not beginning with a nonzero power of $a$ either is empty or begins with a nonzero power of $b$, and then its image under multiplication by $a$ on the left begins with $a$, so it lies in $A$; conversely $aA\subseteq F_2$. Hence $1=m(F_2)=m(A)+m(aA)=2m(A)$ by left invariance, so $m(A)=1/2$. On the other hand $A,bA,b^2A$ are pairwise disjoint subsets of $F_2$ (their elements begin with a nonzero power of $a$, of $b$, and of $b$ respectively, with the $b$-leading sets distinguished by the second letter), so $1=m(F_2)\ge m(A)+m(bA)+m(b^2A)=3m(A)=3/2$, a contradiction. Therefore no left-invariant mean exists and $F_2$ is not amenable.
